title: Aligning Information Theory and Formal Verification: A Lean Formalization of Rate-Distortion Theory
authors: Fubin Yan, Ruxuan Dong, Ruoxuan Shi, Duolei Wang, Kenneth W. Shum
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22404v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models have recently demonstrated an ability to generate substantial mathematical proofs and formalizations, including machine-checked arguments for major open problems and classical theorems. These developments highlight a growing workflow in which AI systems search for proofs while proof assistants certify their correctness. Within information theory, however, formalized libraries remain limited, and existing formalized theorems focus almost exclusively on Shannon's foundational lossless theorems.
  This paper presents the first Lean formalization of core components of rate-distortion theory, a central framework for lossy compression and modern machine-learning analysis. We identify the alignment challenges that arise when translating information-theoretic definitions, such as distortion measures, typicality and achievability, into a proof-assistant setting, and we develop a reusable library of definitions and lemmas faithful to textbook conventions. Our formalization provides a foundation for future AI-assisted proofs in information theory and enables subsequent mechanized developments to build on a coherent, verified infrastructure rather than generating long proofs from scratch.

title: Decomposing URLLC Deadline Failures in Beam-Managed 6G Networks: Implications for Mission-Critical Wireless Systems
authors: Webert Montlouis, Sneihil Gopal
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22411v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mission-critical wireless systems require ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), which sixth-generation (6G) millimeter-wave (mmWave) beam-managed networks are designed to provide. However, the reported URLLC deadline miss rate often masks the specific causes of packet failures. This paper introduces a framework that categorizes missed URLLC packets into three causes: queueing-limited (Q), transmission-limited (T), and beam-tracking-limited (B). Our analysis across ten scenarios with antenna counts from $\mathbf{64}$ to $\mathbf{4096}$ reveals three key findings. First, the dominant cause of missed packets shifts from Q to B when the antenna count exceeds roughly $\mathbf{1825}$. Therefore, operators of hyper-massive arrays should focus on improving beam-tracking accuracy to reduce the miss rate. Second, the beam-sweep period ($T_{\mathrm{sw}}$) significantly affects B-misses, while Q and T remain relatively unchanged. Reducing $T_{\mathrm{sw}}$ from $\mathbf{20}$ms to $\mathbf{10}$ms can cut the B-misses by more than half, without requiring a redesign of the scheduler. Third, Q-misses reach a cumulative distribution function (CDF) of approximately $\mathbf{0.98}$ by $\mathbf{0.8}\,$ms, so modest latency-budget relaxation can accommodate most overruns. In contrast, B-misses remain unsaturated at $\mathbf{12}\,$ms, making them difficult to accommodate within practical application-layer latency limits. Overall, this framework transforms an ambiguous aggregate miss-rate metric into a clear three-way diagnostic tool that directly informs remedial actions for network operators.

title: GPU-Accelerated Robust MA--RIS Pre-Optimization for Communication and Target Illumination
authors: Tran Le Dung, Ho Viet Duc Luong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22431v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer strong spatial control for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), but repeatedly adapting MA positions and RIS phases to each channel realization can be impractical. This letter develops a GPU-accelerated robust pre-optimization framework that jointly selects slow-timescale MA geometry and RIS phases and returns a reusable Pareto set balancing expected worst-user rate and transmit-side worst-target illumination. The illumination objective measures directional transmitted power rather than complete echo-detection or parameter-estimation performance. The proposed Regime-Aware Multiobjective Pre-optimization (RAMP) preserves regime-specific Pareto populations, regulates cross-regime mating using Pareto-survival feedback, and constructs a worst-regime robust archive. Numerical results demonstrate competitive robust Pareto quality against the considered evolutionary baselines while avoiding online physical re-optimization.

title: Local Projected Controllability of Nonlocal Continuity Equations
authors: Elena Goncharova, Nikolay Pogodaev, Maxim Staritsyn
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22550v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We formulate and study the problem of local projected controllability (LPC) for characteristic solutions of controlled nonlocal continuity (transport) equations on the space of probability measures over a separable Banach space. The task is motivated in particular by self-interacting models in machine learning, whose action can be represented as controlled dynamics of the probability distribution over input data, while the actual output is given by a finite-dimensional vector of features extracted from the terminal distribution by a possibly nonlinear observation map. Given a fixed finite family of velocity fields which may depend on the transported measure, we ask whether the reachable values of the observable vector fill a neighborhood of its reference value. Our approach is to lift the transport equation in the space of measures to an ordinary differential equation on a Banach space of maps. This representation makes it possible to employ the machinery of Lie brackets developed for Banach manifolds, while the resulting sufficient condition for LPC can be formulated directly on the space of measures.

title: Hausdorff Matrices on the BMOA and Bloch spaces
authors: Petros Galanopoulos, Alejandro Mahillo, Jesus Oliva-Maza, Aristomenis G. Siskakis
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22554v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We determine the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators $\mathcal{H}_\mu$ on BMOA and the Bloch space $\mathscr{B}$, for suitable finite positive Borel measures $\mu$ on $(0,1]$.

title: Embedding theorems for Herz-Type Sobolev spaces on domains
authors: Douadi Drihem
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22570v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we further investigate the properties of Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains, which unify and generalize the classical Sobolev spaces. In particular, we establish several Sobolev-type embedding theorems for these spaces. Moreover, by means of a suitable example, we show that some of the assumptions imposed on the parameters are optimal.

title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
authors: Alexander Chervov, Ilia Gaiur, Sergey Galkin, Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk, Volodya Rubtsov, Shamil Shakirov
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22571v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.

title: Computing Fr\'echet on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
authors: Ian McPherson, Mauro Maggioni
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22592v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fr\'echet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fr\'echet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.

title: On strongly coherent confidence envelopes for the false discoveries
authors: Romain P\'erier, Gilles Blanchard, Guillermo Durand
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22601v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coherence is a long term notion in the literature of multiple testing. From FWER control multiple testing theory to confidence envelopes on the number of false positives, coherence is a desirable property for multiple testing procedures. However, we show in this article that coherence is not a sufficient property to ensure that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via an interpolation mechanism. We introduce a new no- tion, the notion of strong coherence, which is a stronger property than coherence and ensures that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via the interpolation mech- anisms considered in the literature. Finally, we provide a uniform improvement of the confidence envelope from Durand et al. (2020) that is computable in polynomial time and demonstrate the improvement on simulated data.

title: Distributed Optimization over Simplicial Complexes via Topological Dirac Synchronization
authors: Christian D. Rodr\'iguez-Camargo, Andr\'es F. Urquijo-Rodr\'iguez, Eduardo A. Mojica-Nava
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22628v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a distributed optimization framework for systems with higher-order interactions represented by simplicial and cell complexes. Specializing global topological Dirac synchronization to gradient flows of strongly convex local objectives, we show that the synchronized equilibrium coincides with the minimizer of the aggregate cost, without Lagrange multipliers, dual variables, or saddle-point dynamics. Orientation-equivariant convex terms and cell-dependent dimensional targets allow the optimal state to be nonzero, as determined by joint per-dimension optimality conditions. Our algorithm couples signals across dimensions through the Dirac operator: nodes interact with edges, edges with nodes and faces, and faces with edges, enabling information exchange beyond graph-Laplacian methods. In the isotropic case, a Master Stability Function analysis yields a necessary and sufficient condition for local exponential stability: the product of the directional coupling strengths must be below the squared ratio of the strong convexity parameter to the spectral radius of the complex. A weighted Lyapunov argument accounting for non-normal Dirac coupling establishes global exponential convergence at the same rate. Finally, we identify a topological admissibility condition ensuring invariance of the synchronization manifold and coherent convergence of cells to the optimum, with no counterpart in classical graph-based distributed optimization.

title: Absolute continuity of invariant measures for random diffeomorphisms
authors: Aaron Brown, Alex Eskin, Simion Filip, Federico Rodriguez Hertz
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22654v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop criteria showing that invariant measures for random walks generated by diffeomorphisms of manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Our assumptions are first, that there is a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum of the random walk, and second, that the conditionals of the invariant measure along the appropriate (partial) stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class.

title: A Spectral Approach to Fixed Points in Product Spaces
authors: Aleksander \'Cwiszewski, Wojciech Kryszewski
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22666v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study fixed points of mappings on finite products of Banach spaces whose coordinatewise Lipschitz estimates are controlled by a nonnegative matrix $A$. Our main result states that, if every coordinate space has normal structure and $r(A)\leq1$, then every such self-mapping of a nonempty weakly compact convex set has a fixed point. The result is a direct generalization of the Browder--G\"ohde--Kirk principle. The proof combines classical nonexpansive fixed point theory with Frobenius normal form, passing successively to coordinate projections and invariant fibres. As preparation, the classical reduction of Perov's theorem to the Banach contraction principle through adapted lattice norms is revisited. Applications include a Dirichlet boundary value problem for systems of abstract second order differential equations and a periodic problem for ODE systems satisfying one-sided matrix estimates.

title: Optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems
authors: Tyler Jensen, David I Ketcheson, Lajos L\'oczi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We design and test several new optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods, and provide new and improved five-step methods. We also develop new methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for some of the new methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.

title: Universal operators: topology and consequences of ISP failure
authors: Jo\~ao Carmo, Ben-Hur Eidt, Waleed Noor
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22694v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Assuming a negative answer to the invariant subspace problem for separable complex Hilbert spaces, we prove that every universal operator has a continuum of minimal infinite-dimensional invariant subspaces with pairwise trivial intersections. These subspaces can be chosen so that the restrictions are invertible and their powers decay at any prescribed geometric rate. For an affine composition operator on the Hardy space \(H^2(\D)\), we derive restrictions on the zeros, inner factors and Hardy regularity of generators, and construct minimal models with radial vanishing of any prescribed finite order. Independently of the invariant subspace problem, we identify the norm interior, closure and boundary of the universal operator class. Its interior is the Caradus--Pozzi class, its closure is the complement of the upper semi-Fredholm class, and its boundary consists of the operators that are neither upper nor lower semi-Fredholm.

title: On exponential stability of generalized linear functional differential equations
authors: Leonid Berezansky, Elena Braverman
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22696v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a general approach to uniform exponential stability for a broad class of linear functional differential equations with Volterra operators. The considered class includes delay differential equations, integro-differential equations, equations with distributed delays, vector equations, and systems of scalar functional differential equations. Standard assumptions on the equation are relaxed to include measurable parameters. Some results remain valid for equations with unbounded delays and oscillatory coefficients and kernels. For all the above mentioned classes of equations, explicit uniform exponential stability tests are obtained.

title: Area Theorems for Quantum Error Correction
authors: Avijit Mandal, Mert G\"{o}kduman, Henry D. Pfister
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22710v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) and generalized EXIT (GEXIT) area theorems provide fundamental conservation laws that connect the rate of classical codes to the performance of maximum-a-posteriori decoding on binary memoryless channels. In this work, we generalize these area theorems to quantum error correction. We first develop a coset-entropy formalism for nested linear codes, where the message specifies a coset and encoder randomization selects a codeword within that coset. The area under the resulting coset (G)EXIT function equals the normalized dimension of the quotient. For stabilizer codes, the measured syndrome restricts the Pauli error but does not always determine its logical effect, and the remaining uncertainty is an entropy over logical correction classes. We show that this entropy equals a classical coset entropy associated with the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it. The resulting quantum GEXIT function has area equal to the number of encoded qubits per channel use for any stabilizer code, and this applies to the depolarizing channel through its joint four-valued Pauli-error distribution. For CSS codes on the quantum erasure channel and under independent bit- and phase-flip noise, the logical correction problem separates into two binary coset-decoding problems. On the quantum erasure channel, the duality between the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it gives a folding identity at complementary erasure probabilities. Using this and the area theorem, we derive an upper bound on the rate of code families with vanishing logical error probability that matches the capacity of the quantum erasure channel. For the depolarizing channel, we also derive a rate-dependent converse, using a connection between correction-class entropy and coherent information to establish an inequality involving the complementary channel.

title: UAV Rotatable Antenna under Rotation Delay
authors: Yinmei Xie, Chiya Zhang, Chunlong He, Weizheng Zhang, Wei Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22777v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rotatable antennas (RAs) can improve wireless link performance by adjusting their boresight directions. However, existing RA studies generally assume instantaneous antenna reconfiguration, whereas mechanical rotation incurs non-negligible delay in practical deployment. To address this issue, we develop a rotation-delay-aware communication model for finite communication slots, where mechanical rotation directly reduces the time available for data transmission. This model reveals a fundamental tradeoff between the communication gain achieved through RA reorientation and the associated transmission-time loss. Accordingly, we formulate a rotation-delay-aware joint design of RA orientations and transmit beamforming to maximize the minimum effective transmission rate. For the single-user system, under a sufficient condition for strict concavity, the global optimum falls into one of three regimes: no rotation, partial rotation, and full rotation. A closed-form approximation is derived using a second-order expansion. For the multi-user system, we separate rotation-budget selection from fixed-budget max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) optimization. An analytic-gradient zero-forcing (AG-ZF) algorithm is then developed for low-complexity joint RA orientation and rotation-budget optimization. The results show that explicitly accounting for mechanical rotation delay is essential for finite-slot RA-enabled UAV communications, and that the proposed designs effectively balance reconfiguration gain and transmission-time loss while achieving favorable effective-rate performance with low computational complexity.

title: Single-Letterization of Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Static Time-Invariant Control (STIC) Systems
authors: Eray Unsal Atay, Venkat Chandrasekaran, Victoria Kostina
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22789v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In settings such as online recommendation platforms, medical decision-making with interim summaries, and stochastic control with static plants, the underlying system is often static so that the next state depends only on the most recent action. Moreover, the true system state is high-dimensional and cannot be observed directly, so actions must be selected based on information received through a rate-limited communication link, which constrains the control performance. This leads to a fundamental rate-cost tradeoff$\unicode{x2014}$the minimum communication rate required to achieve a prescribed average control cost. We study this tradeoff for a class of static systems we term static time-invariant control (STIC) systems, namely, control systems in which the next state depends on the history only through the most recent control action via a time-invariant kernel. For general control systems$\unicode{x2014}$not necessarily static or time-invariant$\unicode{x2014}$our prior work characterized this tradeoff through the limit of a sequence of directed-information minimization problems. However, the dimension of these problems grows with the time horizon, making the limiting formulation computationally intractable. In the present paper, we show for STIC systems that this growing-size formulation admits a single-letter characterization. This identifies STIC systems as the control-side counterpart of Noisy Output is the STate (NOST) channels$\unicode{x2014}$one of the few channel models whose feedback capacity admits a single-letter characterization. This yields, to our knowledge, the first constant-size convex characterization of the rate$\unicode{x2013}$cost tradeoff beyond linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control.

title: Marchal-type lemmas for the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with their applications
authors: Kuo-chang Chen, Guowei Yu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22849v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The direct methods of calculus of variations have had a great success in the classical Newtonian $N$-body problem in this century. First in finding periodic solutions and more recently in the existence of parabolic, hyperbolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions. The foundation of many of these results is Marchal's lemma, which guarantee's fixed-end local minimizers are collision-free and hence classical solutions of the $N$-body problem. Meanwhile almost no result is available in the restricted problem through the direct methods of calculus of variations, mainly due to the lack of a Marchal-type lemma.
  In this paper such a lemma and its variation will be obtained for the restricted problem. We then apply them to the restricted problem to study unbounded (hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic and bi-parabolic) solutions, and bounded (periodic and quasi-periodic) solutions. We emphasize that the extension to the restricted case does not follow from the standard arguement for the unrestricted case.

title: Geometric multigrid preconditioners for unfitted discretisations of the de Rham complex
authors: Santiago Badia, Jordi Manyer
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose two families of multigrid preconditioners for unfitted finite element discretisations of the Riesz maps of the de Rham complex, in H(grad), H(curl) and H(div), stabilised by cell aggregation. The first is a geometric multigrid method applied directly to the unfitted operators, on a hierarchy of background meshes that share the same boundary representation. Its smoothers are star patches built on the aggregated mesh, so that each patch captures the kernel of the stabilisation. The second is a multilevel auxiliary-space preconditioner that combines a patch smoother localised around the cut cells with the body-fitted problem on the active mesh, which is in turn solved by a non-nested geometric multigrid method. Both are used as building blocks of block-diagonal preconditioners for the mixed Hodge Laplacians. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on geometries with a controlled cut fraction and on general geometries, show iteration counts that are robust with respect to the cut configuration, the mesh size and the number of levels. We also report results for higher-order discretisations, weakly imposed Dirichlet boundary conditions and a face-based stabilisation.

title: Continuity of biaccessibility dimension for polynomials
authors: Yan Gao
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22870v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a polynomial $f$ of degree $d\geq 2$, its biaccessible set $B(f)$ consists of angles whose external rays are smooth and land at a point receiving at least two smooth external rays. We prove that the function $f\mapsto {\rm dim}_H(B(f))$ is continuous on the entire space of degree-$d$ polynomials. Therefore $(\log d){\rm dim}_H (B(f))$ gives a continuous extension of classical core entropy from the postcritically finite case to all polynomials of degree $d$.

title: Solving the Tikhonov Regularization of the Total Least Squares Problem by matrix simultaneous diagonalization via congruence
authors: Van-Bong Nguyen, Thi Ngan Nguyen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22880v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We are concerned with solving the Tikhonov regularization of the total least squares (TRTLS)
  which minimizes a sum of a quadratic fractional function and a nonnegative penalty quadratic form.
  If the penalty is nonsingular, the problem is attained and has been solved efficiently. However,
  if the penalty is singular, the problem becomes much more complicated, it may not be attained.
  In this paper we explore the property of simultaneously diagonalizable via congruence
  of matrices to make a change of variables and transform the problem into one of three tractable formats. Each of which is then
  thorough analyzed.

title: Compact Toeplitz Operators and the Geometry of Fixed-Radius Averages
authors: Pan Ma, Zhaoxi Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22893v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We characterize compact Toeplitz operators with bounded complex-valued symbols on the Bergman space of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain with $C^2$ boundary. For any fixed $R>0$, the operator $T_f$ is compact if and only if the Euclidean-volume averages of $f$ over Bergman geodesic balls of radius $R$ tend to zero at the boundary. This answers Zhu's fixed-radius question affirmatively on the unit ball. On the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$, $n\ge2$, averages over products of Bergman discs of fixed radii characterize compactness, whereas averages over genuine Bergman geodesic balls need not. For every sufficiently small fixed radius, we construct a bounded real-valued symbol, smooth in the domain, whose geodesic-ball averages tend to zero along every sequence approaching the boundary, while its Berezin transform converges to a positive value along one such sequence. Boundary scaling reduces the strongly pseudoconvex case to a uniqueness problem for fixed-radius ball averages on complex hyperbolic space. We prove the required uniqueness theorem under a sharp decay condition expressed in terms of a Busemann height function.

title: Gaussian Identification in MIMO Channels
authors: Mohammad Javad Salariseddigh, Christian Deppe
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22931v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the identification capacity of discrete-time Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels under per-antenna, per-symbol peak-amplitude constraints. We establish upper and lower bounds on the identification capacity that scale linearly with the channel rank $r.$ The number of reliably identifiable messages can grow super-exponentially with blocklength $n,$ following $M_n(R)=2^{(n\log n)R},$ where $R$ is an achievable rate. The channel rank provides a spatial-multiplexing advantage, enabling higher achievable rates and, consequently, stronger super-exponential codebook growth. These results characterize the rank-dependent gain in achievable identification performance.

title: Rigorous verification of period-doubling bifurcations in maps
authors: Olivier H\'enot, Jean-Philippe Lessard
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22986v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a computer-assisted approach for proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps $x \mapsto f(x,\lambda)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We solve a square augmented system, called the period-doubling map, whose unknowns are the fixed point, the parameter, the right eigenvector attached to the eigenvalue $-1$, the left eigenvector with its eigenvalue, and the vector which describes the center manifold to second order. A contraction argument gives a solution close to a numerical approximation, at which the Jacobian is invertible. The determinant of this Jacobian factors into a simple expression, so that it is nonzero exactly when $1$ is not an eigenvalue and $-1$ is a simple eigenvalue crossing the unit circle transversally. Apart from the sign of the cubic normal-form coefficient, computed afterwards, it remains to check with Gershgorin disks that no other eigenvalue lies on the unit circle. The method is applied to a $10$-mode Galerkin projection of the Kot--Schaffer growth-dispersal model, for which we prove a supercritical period-doubling bifurcation.

title: A note on the non-wandering dynamics in the $n$-fold symmetric products
authors: Ma\v{s}a {\DJ}ori\'c
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23058v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We construct a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set consists of a single fixed point, while the induced map $F_n(f)$ possesses infinitely many (non-fixed) non-wandering points.

title: Achievable Rate Region Characterization of Rotatable Antenna-assisted Interference Channel
authors: Junran Pei, Guangji Chen, Qingqing Wu, Qiaoyan Peng, Wei Cai
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23067v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper characterizes the achievable rate region of a rotatable antenna (RA)-assisted multiple-input single-output (MISO) interference channel. We exploit the additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) offered by the dynamic orientation of RAs to simultaneously enhance the desired signal and suppress interference, thereby significantly enlarging the achievable rate region of the interference network. To this end, we invoke the rate-profile technique to formulate a sum-rate maximization problem for jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming and the array rotation, subject to the practical mechanical constraints of the RAs. For the special case of a two-receiver scenario, we introduce the concept of subspace correlation coefficient to derive closed-form solutions for the optimal RA rotation angles and transmit beamforming vectors. Inspired by the insights obtained in the two-receiver special case, we propose an efficient two-step optimization framework to obtain a high-quality solution for the general multi-receiver case. In particular, the array rotation angle of each transmitter is optimized to minimize the leakage interference to non-associated receivers. With the optimized array rotation angles, the optimal transmit beamforming is obtained by invoking the second order cone programming based approach. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution achieves near-optimal performance and that integrating RAs effectively simplifies transceiver designs by enabling simple maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming with negligible performance loss.

title: Unified Geometric--Kinematic Laws of Mobility in 3D Cellular Networks
authors: Tian Shi, Minghua Xia
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23075v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mobility in three-dimensional (3D) cellular networks induces frequent handovers and random sojourn times for aerial users. Analyzing these events is challenging because they jointly depend on user trajectories and random service-boundary geometry. This paper develops a unified geometric--kinematic framework in which service regions form a stationary random tessellation, their boundaries constitute a random closed set, and user motion follows a cruise--turn mobility model. Under the stated stationarity, isotropy, and independence conditions, the handover rate satisfies the exact law \(H=(S_V/2)\bar v\), where \(S_V\) is the specific surface area and \(\bar v\) is the long-run mean speed. The forward boundary-distance distribution provides the local geometric input to an effective-traversal approximation for the mean remaining sojourn time. These results link global and local geometric descriptors to complementary mobility metrics. Combining the handover law with link coverage yields a handover-aware effective spectral efficiency for base station (BS) density selection and service-architecture comparison. We then specialize the framework to Poisson--Voronoi single-BS service and Poisson--Delaunay four-BS coordinated multi-point service; under both models, the handover rate scales as \(\lambda^{1/3}\bar v\). Numerical results corroborate the exact handover expressions, assess the sojourn-time approximations, and show how user speed and interruption duration affect the preferred density and architecture.

title: Geometry-Aware Latent Representation Learning for Drag Coefficient Prediction of Irregular Particles
authors: Zihao Li, Shota Deguchi, Mitsuteru Asai, Shunhua Chen, Naoto Mitsume
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23087v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Predicting the drag coefficient $C_\mathrm{d}$ of irregular particles requires representing their complex three-dimensional geometry in a form suitable for predictive models. Empirical drag correlations and many data-driven models represent particle geometry through a small set of hand-crafted shape descriptors. Geometric differences omitted by these descriptors are unavailable to the predictor. We propose a variational autoencoder-multilayer perceptron (VAE-MLP) framework that learns a latent representation directly from voxelized particle geometry. Geometry reconstruction and drag coefficient prediction jointly guide the learning of this representation. We compare VAE-MLP with a descriptor-based MLP (Descriptor-MLP) and established empirical correlations using CFD data for synthetic particle geometries at Reynolds numbers of 10--200. When the evaluated geometric variations are represented in the training data, the two learned models achieve comparable accuracy for regular ellipsoids, while VAE-MLP yields lower errors for irregular particles. When high-order surface perturbations are excluded from training, VAE-MLP achieves lower overall mean absolute relative error in all five training runs. At the strongest tested perturbation, the mean errors across these runs are 4.97% for VAE-MLP and 9.88% for Descriptor-MLP. These results support learning geometric representations directly from particle geometry to improve drag prediction for the irregular geometries and unseen surface perturbations examined here.

title: Time-optimal vaccination in state-dependent SIR models: a single switch criterion and numerical examples outside its regime
authors: Yeachan Park, Jiwoong Jang, Yeoneung Kim
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23095v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In a susceptible, infected, and recovered (SIR) model with constant rates, a time-optimal vaccination policy has at most one switch from no vaccination to maximal vaccination. We allow the transmission and recovery rates $\beta(S,I)$ and $\gamma(S,I)$ to depend on the state. If $\beta+I\partial_I\beta>0$ and $G:=\partial_S(\beta S-\gamma)>0$ throughout the forward invariant state space, then every optimal control is bang-bang with at most one switch. The incidence condition allows the transmission coefficient to decrease with prevalence. The Pontryagin analysis shows that $G$, the sensitivity of per capita infected growth to the susceptible fraction, and the infected costate together determine the crossing direction of the switching function. We also prove existence of an optimal control, derive explicit a priori upper bounds on the eradication time and characterize the switching time by an optimization over one variable. For parameter sets that violate $G>0$, numerical optimization gives controls with two switches and smaller eradication times than the computed minima over the single switch family. These computations provide a reproducible numerical counterexample to an unrestricted single switch claim. In a prescribed parameter sweep satisfying $G>0$, delayed vaccination reduces the eradication time relative to immediate full vaccination by more than $1\%$ in $10.9\%$ of the cases, with a maximum reduction of $26.3\%$. In examples near this maximum, the delay increases peak prevalence by more than an order of magnitude and cumulative incidence more than fourfold. Hence minimizing eradication time does not in general minimize epidemiological burden.

title: Watanabe's Learning Coefficients in Item Response Theory
authors: Joe Suzuki, Takumi Ikejiri, Yuki Kurumadani
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23102v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the joint-parameter two-parameter logistic (2PL) model in item response theory, in which both item parameters and respondent abilities are treated as unknown fixed parameters. We first characterize its singular structure through the Fisher information matrix. The parameterization has an inherent scale indeterminacy; when all discrimination parameters are nonzero and the ability parameters are not all equal, its tangent direction is the only null direction and the quotient model is locally regular. We then classify the additional rank deficiencies caused by zero discrimination parameters and degenerate ability configurations. This classification separates the strata governed by a nondegenerate quadratic approximation from those requiring an analysis of higher-order product singularities. Under an asymptotic regime in which the numbers of items and respondents are fixed and the number of independent response matrices tends to infinity, we derive explicit local and global learning coefficients and multiplicities for every realizable true response distribution. The global formulas depend only on the true response probabilities, including cases in which some probabilities equal \(1/2\) or are constant across respondents. These results extend previous calculations restricted to nonzero true discrimination parameters and provide the quantities required for applying sBIC to the joint-parameter 2PL model.
  Key Words: item response theory; two-parameter logistic model; singular learning theory; learning coefficient; real log canonical threshold; Fisher information matrix; sBIC.

title: Generalization of Navascu\'es' $\alpha$-fractal operator on lifted Sierpi\'nski gasket
authors: Gurubachan, S. Verma, V. V. M. S. Chandramouli
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23159v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The primary objective of the present article is to extend Navascu\'es' class of $\alpha$-fractal interpolation functions ($\alpha$-FIFs) from a Euclidean domain to a non-Euclidean domain. Precisely, we consider the lifted Sierpi\'nski gasket $\big(\widetilde{SG}\big)$, which is a subset of the first Heisenberg group equipped with a \textit{non-Euclidean metric} (popularly known as the Heisenberg metric), and demonstrate the existence of the class of $\alpha$-FIFs in the continuous space on $\widetilde{SG}$. Subsequently, we derive certain conditions on the parameters so that the same class lies in the H\"{o}lder space on $\widetilde{SG}$. Next, we extend the theory of Navascu\'es' $\alpha$-fractal operator from the Euclidean space to the Heisenberg space, and we also report several properties of the same operator. Additionally, we discuss certain dimensional results of the graphs of the functions with respect to the Heisenberg metric besides the Euclidean metric. We also cover some of the dimensional preserving and the set-valued results corresponding to the dimension of the graphs of the functions.

title: Stability and Error Estimates for Convolution Quadrature under Radial Symbol Bounds
authors: Jingchuang Ren, Haibin Su
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23163v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop stability and error estimates for multistep convolution quadrature (CQ) under general radial bounds on the Laplace symbol. Instead of the classical single-power condition $|F(z)|\leq M|z|^{-\mu}$, we assume $|F(z)|\leq C\Phi(|z|)$ and consider two classes of radial functions: monotone bounds satisfying a scaling condition and regularly varying bounds with locally bounded above and away from zero. For strongly $A(\alpha)$-stable multistep methods, we derive approximation and stability estimates for the CQ weights, as well as error bounds for power-type inputs $g_\beta(t)=t^{\beta-1}/\Gamma(\beta)$ with $\beta>0$. These estimates explicitly retain the dependence on the memory law through the factor $\Phi(t_n^{-1})$. The framework accommodates symbols whose behavior cannot be described by a global single-power. It also preserves slowly varying and multiscale factors that would be lost under a coarser power majorant. The theory is applied to fractional viscoelastic models, distributed-order operators, and logarithmic-power memory operators. Numerical experiments with backward Euler and second-order backward differentiation CQ confirm the expected temporal convergence orders for direct responses. Complementary evolution examples demonstrate the corresponding temporal behavior for smooth and nonsmooth initial data.

title: Nondimensionalization, Variational Inequalities and Uncertainty Quantification in a Morphoelastic Model for Burn Injury Healing
authors: Wilbert den Hertog, Fred Vermolen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23177v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mathematical modelling of burn injury healing involves coupling biological processes with mechanical deformation, resulting in computationally stiff, nonlinear partial differential equations that severely limit the scalability of existing numerical solutions. We present a computational framework addressing these challenges. By nondimensionalizing the model and performing scaling analysis, we show that chemotaxis and inertia are negligible, permitting a quasi-static momentum approach. To enforce non-negativity constraints, we implement a Variational Inequality formulation using the Finite Element Method in FEniCSx, and verify it via numerical convergence studies and mass balances. We identify high-order parameter interactions, specifically equilibrium collagen density and signalling dynamics, as the primary drivers of solver stability. A sensitivity analysis of nearly four million simulations reveals that isolated parameter variations predominantly govern the maximum wound contraction. In contrast, higher-order interactions determine the timing of maximum contraction and the permanent contracture. However, no significant pairwise parameter interactions were found, suggesting that the model's behaviour is governed by higher-order interactions, highlighting the inherent complexity of the wound-healing process.

title: Critical cusp cancellation and analytic response for a Bernoulli random interval map
authors: Davrbek Oltiboev, Furqat Vafoyev
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23180v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that the critical cusp exponent $\beta=-1/2$ admits $W^{2,1}$ invariant densities in an explicit family of expanding full-branch interval maps. The usual estimates exclude this exponent because two zero-order coefficients in the second derivative of the transfer operator are individually non-integrable. Their signed combination, however, contains the factor $\beta(2\beta+1)$ for a pure power cusp. We exploit its cancellation at $\beta=-1/2$ to prove a $W^{2,1}$ Lasota--Yorke inequality and a spectral gap for the explicit family. We also identify a separate obstruction caused by an interior cusp value. As an application, a small Bernoulli probability perturbation between two fixed maps has a stationary density that depends real-analytically on the perturbation parameter in $W^{2,1}$, with explicit formulas for all response derivatives.

title: Multilevel Gaussian Processes with Applications to Inverse Problems
authors: Stjepan Salatovic, Aretha L. Teckentrup, Sebastian Krumscheid
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23202v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a multilevel Gaussian process (GP) regression framework for approximating functions that are accessible only through a hierarchy of approximations of increasing accuracy and computational cost. One example is the response surface of a parametrized partial differential equation, where the hierarchy arises from the resolution of the numerical solver. Modeling level increments independently with Mat\'ern-kernel GPs and allocating samples flexibly across discretization levels yields substantial computational savings over single-level GP regression. We derive $L^2$ convergence rates for the posterior mean and variance, accounting for maximum likelihood estimation of the marginal variance and for kernel misspecification. When increment regularity or solver cost is unknown a priori, an adaptive sequential-design algorithm with cost-adapted active learning criteria allocates samples across levels. We apply the surrogate to Bayesian inverse problems, for which Hellinger distance bounds between the true and approximate posteriors are known. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical rates and the resulting computational savings.

title: Synthesis of the Transient Behaviour of Optimization Algorithms for Strongly Convex Objective Functions
authors: Adel Abdelsamed, Dennis Gramlich, Christian Ebenbauer, Carsten W. Scherer
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23206v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the transient behavior of first-order optimization methods for unconstrained minimization of smooth and strongly convex objective functions. These methods are modelled as linear systems over finite-time intervals embedded in feedback with the gradient nonlinearity. By characterizing the function class through discrete-time Zames-Falb integral quadratic constraints, we employ a robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ control framework to obtain convex semidefinite programs certifying tight worst-case bounds on the terminal distance to the optimizer. Building on the same formulation, we derive a convex synthesis procedure for a transient-optimal method that achieves the optimal finite-horizon bounds and guarantees error reduction over any prescribed number of steps. The framework naturally extends to delayed gradient measurements, enabling both transient performance analysis and synthesis of optimal algorithms under feedback delays.

title: On Mbekhta's conjecture and pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces
authors: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23229v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of $\cc(T)$, $\cc(T)+\qn(T)$ and $\Ran(T)+\qn(T)$, as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.

title: On the complexification of $ q $-deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups
authors: Heon Lee, Christian Voigt
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For the quantised algebra of functions on a simply connected compact semisimple Lie group, we study the relationship between the primitive spectrum, topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on Hilbert spaces, and quantum holomorphic evaluations induced via the Drinfeld double. In terms of the Joseph stratification of the primitive spectrum, we prove a sharp dichotomy: primitive ideals in homogeneous strata always arise as kernels of topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on a Hilbert space, whereas those in inhomogeneous strata do not admit any such realisations. We further show that, unlike in the classical situation, quantum holomorphic evaluations typically fail to be topologically irreducible, and that their kernels do not determine the primitive spectrum. Finally, we describe the Iwasawa decomposition of the Drinfeld double in terms of polynomial functions, extending work by Podle\'s-Woronowicz for the quantum Lorentz group to all complex semisimple quantum groups, and clarifying the structure of quantum holomorphic evaluations.

title: A configurational numerical viscosity for thermodynamically compatible finite volume schemes of compressible multiphase flows
authors: Davide Ferrari, Ilya Peshkov, Michael Dumbser
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider the fluid subsystem of a variationally derived hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (HTC) model of compressible multiphase flows. Its total energy is in general not convex in the natural state variables, so a scalar numerical viscosity acting on them need not produce non-negative entropy. Reformulating the equations in terms of the volume fractions separates changes in the amount of each phase from changes in its intrinsic state. This guides the construction of a configurational numerical viscosity in phase variables, in which the energy is convex, while the scheme retains the structure of the HTC model. At the semi-discrete level, the new schemes satisfy: I) local conservation of the phase masses, the mixture momentum and the total energy; II) a cell entropy inequality whose production is non-negative face by face and phase by phase, with no convexity assumption in the evolved variables and no clipping; III) positivity of the partial densities and volume fractions under explicit time-step conditions; IV) exact preservation of contact equilibria; V) equivalence with a scheme for the density-weighted volume fractions. The key ingredients are: i) an exact decomposition of the jump of each phase across a face into a configurational part, dissipated with the material speed, and an intrinsic part, dissipated with the acoustic speed; ii) an exchange form of this dissipation between neighbouring cells, with non-negative weights; iii) a side-wise transfer of the dissipation to the evolved variables through the chain rule of each cell, which turns the energy defects into Bregman divergences of the single-fluid energies; iv) a thermodynamic correction of the reversible part built in the phase variables. Properties I)-V) are proved and verified numerically, including a shock tube in which the Rusanov viscosity produces negative entropy and a shock-water column interaction.

title: A Class of R\'enyi-based Concentration Metrics for Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry in Multilayer Perceptrons
authors: Juan Carlos Fern\'andez, Asunci\'on Jim\'enez-Cordero, Jos\'e Francisco Paris
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23267v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The interpretability of artificial intelligence models has become a central concern, especially for black-box models such as multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry has recently emerged as a framework for analysing the internal representations of these networks, by examining how the hidden layer locally responds to changes in the input through the minors of its Jacobian. The degree to which a few of these minors dominate the rest, known as their concentration, has so far been measured with the Participation Ratio. Although this metric has useful properties, its maximum value depends on the size of the network, so a given value cannot be read as high or low concentration without reference to the architecture. To overcome this limitation, in this paper we propose the $\alpha$-RC metrics, a family of R\'enyi-based concentration measures that compare the normalized magnitudes of the minors with the uniform distribution through the R\'enyi divergence of order $\alpha$. All the metrics in the family are bounded between 0 and 1 regardless of the architecture, with 0 indicating that the magnitude is evenly spread over the minors and 1 that it is carried by a single one. Moreover, the metrics are non-decreasing in $\alpha$, and for $\alpha$ = 2 they reduce to an explicit transformation of the Participation Ratio. Computational experiments with single-hidden-layer MLPs trained on a synthetic dataset show the benefits of our proposal.

title: A Generalized Half-Singleton Bound for List Decoding of Insertion/Deletion Errors
authors: Neehar Verma, Camilla Hollanti, Razane Tajeddine
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23270v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive an upper bound on the rate of a linear code capable of list decoding from insertion and deletion errors. Subsequently, we show that a linear code can list decode from at most $n - \frac{L}{L+1}k + 1$ insdel errors with fixed list size $L$, and that this bound is strict when the code does not contain the all-ones vector. We also provide a simple construction of codes achieving the optimal rate for any given list size capable of correcting a single insdel error. All the results hold for linear codes over finite fields of size $q \geq 3$.

title: Orthogonal Projections and Assouad Dimension: Resolving Fraser's Questions
authors: Bilel Selmi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23295v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We examine two questions on exceptional orthogonal projections for Assouad dimension. Let $1\le k<d$. The planar packing question, Question 17.8.2, is already answered affirmatively by Wu's countability theorem. Using that theorem, we also describe the distinction between planar sets of Assouad dimension at most $1$ and those of dimension greater than $1$ when they are embedded in higher-dimensional spaces. The computations use elementary Grassmannian geometry; we make no claim of a new planar projection theorem or of an optimal bound for arbitrary higher-dimensional sets.

title: Acceleration Survives Heavy Tails and Generalized Smoothness
authors: Taha El Bakkali El Kadi, Eduard Gorbunov
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23301v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish high-probability accelerated convergence guarantees for convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth optimization with unbiased stochastic gradients under heavy-tailed noise, assuming a central $\alpha$-th noise moment bounded by $\sigma^\alpha$, $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Such guarantees are known under classical $L$-smoothness, but extending them through localization over an $O(R)$-radius ball may introduce an $e^{O(L_1R)}$ factor. We avoid this dependence in two ways. First, a two-phase scheme uses \algname{Clip-SGD} to reach a low-curvature regime, after which clipped stochastic similar triangles (\algname{Clip-SSTM}) attains, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $f(y_K)-f^\star\le\widetilde{\mathcal O}\big(L_0R^2/K^2+\sigma RK^{-(\alpha-1)/\alpha}\big),$ where $R$ bounds the distance from the Phase-II starting point to a minimizer. Second, a modified deterministic weight schedule allows \algname{Clip-SSTM} to start directly from the initial point, controlling the high-curvature transient before recovering acceleration. With the prescribed initialization, both approaches recover the classical accelerated rate, with $L_1$ confined to an accuracy-independent transient, up to logarithmic factors. The two-phase analysis uses two coupled potentials to preserve the low-curvature regime despite momentum; the one-phase analysis controls the initial high-curvature regime using a modified version of the classical SSTM weight schedule.

title: Sieve-free ReLU Bayesian priors with near-minimax posterior contraction
authors: Hien Duy Nguyen, Jacob Westerhout, Julyan Arbel
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23308v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish fractional-posterior contraction for shallow ReLU networks in Gaussian random-design regression with a $\beta$-H\"older target, using priors independent of the sample size and smoothness parameters. For any fixed design law $P_X$ on $[0,1]^d$, we obtain contraction in R\'enyi divergence and, after clipping posterior draws at a bound on the target range, in squared $\mathcal{L}^2(P_X)$ loss at rate $(\log n/n)^{2\beta/(2\beta+d)}$. This matches the classical H\"older minimax rate up to a logarithmic factor. These priors have random finite width and use width-dependent uniform or Gaussian weight distributions, or width-independent Student $t$ distributions, including Cauchy distributions.

title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
authors: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23329v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.

title: Quasi-Monte Carlo based meshfree methods for parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds
authors: Zhijian He, Zhiyuan Hui, Changtao Sheng, Bihao Su, Tao Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23341v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop and analyze a randomized path sampling framework for the pointwise approximation of linear parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds, treating both closed manifolds and manifolds with Dirichlet boundary. Based on the Feynman-Kac representation, we construct a parameter-coordinate retraction-based discretization, referred to as the p-Ret scheme, for the manifold diffusion generated by the uniformly elliptic operator, and use it to formulate the Monte Carlo (MC) and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (RQMC) methods. We derive the local weak consistency of the p-Ret transition and first-order weak convergence of the temporal discretization on closed manifolds. For fixed $h$, we show that RQMC sampling yields asymptotically faster variance decay than standard MC. On closed manifolds, the variance is $o(n^{-1})$ and, under additional regularity, satisfies the sharper bound $O(n^{-2+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon>0$. For Dirichlet problems, despite the discontinuities induced by numerical first exit, nested-uniformly scrambled Sobol' sampling attains $O(n^{-1-1/s+\varepsilon})$ variance for any $\varepsilon>0$ under suitable regularity assumptions, where $s$ denotes the nominal path-space dimension. More notably, we further develop an Array-RQMC strategy based on stepwise low-dimensional randomized point sets and a Hilbert space-filling curve that maps high-dimensional particle states to a one-dimensional ordering, and establish a variance rate of $o(n^{-1})$ under suitable assumptions. Numerical results demonstrate that both RQMC methods reduce variance and root mean square error (RMSE) relative to standard MC and remain effective for manifolds with intrinsic dimension up to $50$.

title: Explicit Oblique Inverses of the Approximate Discrete Radon Transform
authors: Donsub Rim
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23363v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The approximate discrete Radon transform (ADRT) is a fast, hierarchical approximation of the Radon transform whose levels have explicit spectral decompositions, but its Moore-Penrose inverse, needed for data outside the range, has no closed form. We construct explicit left inverses of the ADRT, oblique projections onto its range, that are exact for every choice of their parameters and amplify noise by a constant factor relative to the Moore-Penrose inverse. Realized with polynomial filters on the butterfly structure of the levels, they are fixed linear maps of cost $O(N^{5/2}\log^{3/2}N/\sigma_{\min})$ for an $N\times N$ image, where $\sigma_{\min}$ is the smallest singular value of the ADRT; with the measured growth $\sigma_{\min}\sim N^{1/4}$ this is $O(N^{2.25}\log^{3/2}N)$. A hybrid that keeps the explicit inverse of the cross-quadrant level is cheaper and closer to the Moore-Penrose inverse. In compiled implementations both outperform a polynomial solver of the normal equations from $N=256$ on, and their conditioning is traced to the aliasing of integer-sampled lines.

title: Convergence rate of stochastic gradient descent under {\L}ojasiewicz type condition and polynomially controlled noise
authors: Pawe{\l} W\k{e}grzyn
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23386v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic gradient methods are widely used for solving optimization problems in many scientific fields. Recently, their popularity has risen due to the increase in machine learning's prominence. Their convergence is often studied under the convexity assumption, which is too restrictive in modern applications. In this paper, we investigate the almost sure convergence rate and expectation under a {\L}ojasiewicz-type gradient domination condition. This framework includes both bounded and decaying noise, as well as noise with controlled polynomial growth. The obtained results extend existing convergence by allowing a broader class of noise sequences and explicitly capturing the effect of their asymptotic behavior on the convergence rate and applicability.

title: Accelerated Born series for high-frequency strong scattering by weakly non-radial media
authors: Mirza Karamehmedovi\'c, Faouzi Triki
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23428v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a practical method for accelerating the modified Born series for high-frequency Helmholtz scattering in one, two, and three dimensions. We consider bounded, nonnegative, compactly supported media, allowing small departures from radial symmetry in two and three dimensions. The method selects a single complex relaxation parameter using an approximation of the scattering operator's spectrum. Starting from precomputed eigenvalues for a constant reference medium, we estimate their evolution towards the prescribed radial profile. A leading-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation reduces this spectral propagation to scalar nonlinear equations, followed by a first-order correction for the nonradial part of the medium. The estimated eigenvalues, together with a bound on the omitted spectrum, define a convex minimax problem for selecting the relaxation parameter. This spectral preparation is independent of the source and can therefore be reused for multiple scattering problems in the same medium. Numerical examples demonstrate convergence in strongly scattering cases where the scattering operator has spectral radius greater than one. Comparisons with direct integral-equation and finite-difference solvers assess accuracy, residual convergence, and computation time, and show computational savings at comparable accuracy in selected examples.
